doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Being blessed: boxing, Benny Goodman, Parker and Dizzy
summary: Gibbs says he might have been a boxer but music mattered more; he feels blessed to have played with Goodman, Parker and Dizzy, and stopped touring since he could not keep a steady band.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Yes. So we’ve been at this for about an hour, I’ve really enjoyed this. I want to wrap up with a couple of questions. I wonder if you could have done anything else in your life besides being a musician.

You know I did want to be a boxer at one time but it was either that — but I realized playing music was more important to me. I don’t think there’s anything I actually wanted to do that, you know something Monk? I may have had a lot of mishaps but we all — I’m 97 years old now and we all have had some rainy days. You know. But I am blessed with being, in my 97 years maybe two years of it I would say were dumb, were just something — it’s not I regret, it’s something I couldn’t do anything about. There was a point when I wanted to get custody of my children from somebody who was not fit to have children. I want to finish because this is important. blessed as I was. If you look at the pictures in the book, all those people, first of all Benny Goodman was the King of Swing. When I was 25 years old and he was 42 I played with Benny. After four bars we were the same age. Music has no numbers. Same age. I mean I wrote about this, not only did I play with Charlie Parker but he worked for me one time for four weeks. But Dizzy Gillespie, who was my friend, who heard me play because I worked opposite him a lot of time, I was sitting by a music store when I was working on Operation: Entertainment, I used to go on the road for nine days and I would be in the office writing music. I was sitting in my — I used to hang out in my music store. Dizzy called me and he said, “Terry, James Moody had a Bell’s palsy stroke.” This is in California. “Can you come play with me for ten days?” God, he could have called Teddy, he could have called fifty — this was like heaven when he called, you know. Playing with people I idolized as musicians you know. All the best. Bud Powell. And that’s one of the reasons I gave up playing also, is I couldn’t have a steady band. All the guys who played for me in California, they were great. Tom Ranier, he’s on the academy award show. He wrote for “Dancing with the Stars” — these guys were all busy doing what they call studio work. So they’ll play with me in town, but I can’t travel with them. And playing one night a week, that doesn’t do it for me.
